I'm actually surprised there haven't been more bugs found with blockchain technologies considering how big the push is for Bitcoin to be used as a currency.
I have tried and tried and tried to understand bitcoin and I just can't. How is it "mineable"? How can it have " dust"?

Every transaction is broadcasted and checked against existing balances and such. A bunch of these updates are packed in a block. This block needs to be "encoded" (not actually what is happening but for ease sake ...) with some specific constraints. The network basically brute forces this encoding with random guesses and then checking their answer against a valid answer. This answer is then broadcasted and re-calculated by others. The person that found the answer first is awarded bitcoins for finding the answer. The amount you get decreases over time so there are a finite number of coins, and the difficulty of finding one increases as well.
I still don't get it. I understand all the words you're saying, just not the concept.

In the beginning the makers of Bitcoin decided they needed the currency to initially be distributed evenly between people for it to ever work as a currency. They designed it so that when a computer runs a particular algorithm it has a low, random chance of producing a bitcoin. Running the algorithm is thus called "mining".

Unreasonably small transactions are called dust. If there are a lot of them they can clog the network so they are discouraged by charging a fee for processing them.
